title: Symmetry and Monotonicity of y = -1 / x^2
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Describe the graph of y = -1 / x^2, identify any symmetry of the graph, and specify the intervals on which the function is increasing and decreasing.
finalAnswer: \text{Symmetric about the } y\text{-axis; Decreasing on } (-\infty, 0); \text{ Increasing on } (0, \infty)

steps.title: Determine the Domain and Symmetry
steps.explanation: The function is defined for all x != 0. Since (-x)^2 = x^2, f(-x) = f(x), so the function is even and its graph is symmetric about the y-axis.
steps.why: Even functions have graphs that are mirror images across the y-axis.

steps.title: Analyze Monotonicity on (0, inf)
steps.explanation: For positive x, as x increases, x^2 increases, 1/x^2 decreases toward 0, and therefore -1/x^2 increases from -infinity toward 0.
steps.why: Negating a positive decreasing function on (0, inf) turns it into a negative increasing function.

steps.title: Analyze Monotonicity on (-inf, 0)
steps.explanation: By y-axis symmetry (or direct inequality check), as x increases from -infinity toward 0^-, x^2 decreases toward 0^+, so -1/x^2 decreases from 0^- toward -infinity. Thus f is decreasing on (-inf, 0) and increasing on (0, inf).
steps.why: An even function that is increasing on (0, inf) is necessarily decreasing on (-inf, 0).
